'''Arthur Fales Veinott Jr.''' (October 12, 1934 – December 12, 2012), also known as '''Pete Veinott'''<ref>{{Cite report |url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/do/10.1287/orms.2013.01.27in/full/ |title=In Memoriam - Arthur 'Pete' Veinott Jr. (1934-2012) |date=2019-08-21 |doi=10.1287/orms.2013.01.27in |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref> was an [[United States|American]] operations researcher and academic.

== Early life and education ==

Born in [[Boston, Massachusetts]] on October 12, 1934.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=INFORMS |title=Veinott, Jr., Arthur F. |url=https://www.informs.org/Explore/History-of-O.R.-Excellence/Biographical-Profiles/Veinott-Jr.-Arthur-F |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=INFORMS |language=en-US}}</ref>

He earned his Bachelors of Arts and Science degrees from [[Lehigh University]] in 1956. He studied at Columbia University and earned a Doctorate of Science in 1960, under the supervision of [[Cyrus Derman]].<ref name=":0" />

He died on December 12, 2012.<ref name=":0" />

== Career  ==

He first arrived at Stanford in 1962 and served until 2009.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2012-12-20 |title=Stanford operations research expert Arthur Veinott Dies at 78 {{!}} Stanford University School of Engineering |url=https://engineering.stanford.edu/news/stanford-operations-research-expert-arthur-veinott-dies-78 |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=engineering.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref> During his career, he played a key role in the creation and development of the Department of Operations Research, including serving as department chair from 1975 to 1985.<ref name=":1" />

He founded the journal [[Mathematics of Operations Research]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Arthur Veinott, Jr. {{!}} Management Science and Engineering |url=https://msande.stanford.edu/people/arthur-veinott-jr |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=msande.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* He received the INFORMS [[John von Neumann Theory Prize]] in 2007.<ref name=":2" />
* He was made an inaugural INFORMS Fellow in 2002.<ref name=":2" />
* He was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NAE Website - ARTHUR F. VEINOTT JR. 1934–2012 |url=https://www.nae.edu/260698/ARTHUR-F-VEINOTT-JR-19342012 |access-date=2026-08-13 |website=www.nae.edu}}</ref>
